n3b.ett-lager-inifran.1: A layer from the inside: nine weights and a few fixed calculation rules
n3b.ett-lager-inifran.2: “A layer” in a transformer is not a matrix but the whole block. In Llama-3-8B each layer holds seven weight matrices and two weight vectors, just over 218 million parameters in total.
n3b.ett-lager-inifran.3: Between the weights are steps that have no weights: RoPE, scores, softmax, SiLU and the two additions. They are fixed formulas that are the same in every model of the same kind.
n3b.ett-lager-inifran.4: Click a part of the diagram to see what it does, its shape, and what it is called in a model file.
n3b.ett-lager-inifran.5: weight (learned)calculation rule (no weight)residual stream
n3b.32-lager-i-en-modellfil.2: A model file (safetensors) is essentially a dictionary: name → tensor. Llama-3-8B contains 291 tensors: 9 per layer times 32 layers, plus three outside the layers.
n3b.32-lager-i-en-modellfil.8: All 32 layers have exactly the same names and shapes; only the layer number differs. The values are completely different: each layer has learned its own part of the job. That is why the same code can run in a loop, with a new set of weights on every pass.
n3b.32-lager-i-en-modellfil.9: PyTorch stores a linear weight as [out, in]. That is why k_proj says [1024, 4096], while the course writes [4096, 1024] in the flow direction. It is the same matrix, transposed.
n3b.32-lager-i-en-modellfil.10: A slice of q_proj.weight, 10 × 24 out of 4096 × 4096 numbers:
n3b.32-lager-i-en-modellfil.11: The values in the slices are made up. In a real model they look like noise to the eye, but differ between layers in the same way.

n3b.attention-och-mlp-olika-jobb.1: Attention and the MLP: two completely different jobs
n3b.attention-och-mlp-olika-jobb.2: Think of the residual stream as a table x [T, 4096]: one row per token, one column per dimension.
n3b.attention-och-mlp-olika-jobb.3: Attention moves information between rows. Each token fetches a weighted mix from earlier tokens. That is how “den” can learn something about “Katten”.
n3b.attention-och-mlp-olika-jobb.4: The MLP processes one row at a time. It mixes the dimensions within the row, but can never see other rows. Every row goes through the same MLP weights, one at a time.
n3b.attention-och-mlp-olika-jobb.5: A detail that is easy to miss: even inside attention, the weight matrices Wq, Wk, Wv and Wo work row by row. The only step that crosses rows is P · V.
n3b.attention-och-mlp-olika-jobb.6: attention: mixes along T (between tokens) MLP: mixes along d (within a token)
n3b.attention-och-mlp-olika-jobb.9: Click a row to select a token.
n3b.mlp-n-som-detektorer.2: Every neuron in the MLP is a column in W_gate and a row in W_down. The column in W_gate is a pattern. The dot product with the token’s vector determines how well the vector matches the pattern.
n3b.mlp-n-som-detektorer.3: gate = h · W_gate[:, n] how well does h match? a = SiLU(gate) · up let through if yes ut += a · W_down[n, :] write the neuron’s direction
n3b.mlp-n-som-detektorer.4: So a neuron that fires writes its own direction into the stream. With 14,336 neurons per layer and 32 layers, there is room for a very large number of such rules.
n3b.mlp-n-som-detektorer.5: Turn features of the token’s vector on and off on the right, and see which neurons light up.
n3b.mlp-n-som-detektorer.6: A simplified picture. Real neurons rarely have a clean human meaning; most respond to mixtures of many patterns, and one concept is often spread over many neurons (superposition).

n3b.lager-for-lager.1: Layer by layer: how the answer emerges
n3b.lager-for-lager.2: Because the stream has the same shape in every layer, you can take any intermediate state and send it through the final norm and LM head, as if the model stopped there. The technique is called a logit lens.
n3b.lager-for-lager.3: The result shows how the prediction is built up:
n3b.lager-for-lager.4: Early on, the stream mostly resembles the embedding of the token itself.
n3b.lager-for-lager.5: Halfway through, grammatically plausible continuations appear.
n3b.lager-for-lager.6: Late on, attention has fetched the context and the MLPs have drawn their conclusions, and the right answer takes over.
n3b.lager-for-lager.7: No layer “decides” the answer. Each layer nudges the distribution a little, and the sum of all the nudges is the final one.
n3b.lager-for-lager.8: The numbers are made up to show the pattern. In real models the early layers are often hard to read with a plain logit lens, and variants such as the tuned lens work better.
